Before we dig in, I'll check whether your course materials cover this.

Your course materials don't cover Roman history. They're about calculus, recursion, biology, and physics. So I'll answer from general knowledge and won't tie it to your course.

Historians rarely point to a single cause. Common threads include:
- Political instability, such as frequent civil wars and rapid turnover of emperors
- Economic strain from heavy taxation, inflation, and reliance on a costly army
- Military pressure from migrating and invading groups
- The split into Eastern and Western halves, with the West weaker

Which of these do you think would hurt an empire most, and why?
